summary: Preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (`_0xXXXX` identifiers, junk-string dictionary) and, at npm install time, downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime ZIP from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases (v1.3.13), unpacks it to a temp directory, marks the binary executable, and uses that freshly-downloaded Bun binary to execute the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line Bun-bundled artifact (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) consisting of a rotated hex opcode/string array with a `push/shift` array-rotator (`WV8StW`) and a `fromCodePoint` decoder — not human-readable and unrelated to any math functionality referenced elsewhere in the package (which is otherwise a OneReach CS2.0 CLI). Executing bundled code under a smuggled-in alternate runtime at preinstall bypasses Node-based install-time scanning; the behavior of the executed payload cannot be observed without running it. The declared package purpose (OneReach CLI tooling) has no need for Bun. The `math_init.js` name is a cover-story mismatch against actual contents.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
